name: Alcohol (ethanol)
summary: The exception that teaches the rule. Every other substance here leaves at a rate proportional to how much is present, so it has a half-life. Alcohol saturates its own enzyme almost immediately and then leaves at a near-constant amount per hour, no matter how much you drank. Doubling the dose doubles the time, and nothing speeds it up.
mechanism: Enhances GABA-A inhibition and blocks NMDA glutamate receptors, which together suppress cortical activity from the top down: judgement and inhibition first, then coordination, then memory formation, then the brainstem reflexes that keep you breathing.
vd_note: Alcohol distributes into total body water, so the volume is body water, not whole body mass. Widmark's r: about 0.68 L/kg for men and 0.55 for women, mostly because of differing body-fat fraction. Fat holds almost no water, so for the same weight and dose, more body fat means a higher peak.
elimination_note: Michaelis-Menten with Vmax about 0.22 g/L/h and Km about 0.082 g/L. Because a typical BAC is ten times Km, the enzyme runs essentially flat out and the curve comes down in a straight line of roughly 0.15 to 0.20 g/L per hour (0.015-0.020 %BAC/h). Coffee, cold showers and exercise do not change Vmax.

oral.note: Absorbed from the stomach and especially the small intestine, with an absorption half-life of about 10 minutes on an empty stomach. Some is destroyed before it reaches the blood by gastric alcohol dehydrogenase — first-pass metabolism which is lower in women and lower again on an empty stomach. Note that the time to peak is not a fixed property here: because elimination is saturated from the start, a larger dose peaks later as well as higher.

oral_with_food.note: Food slows gastric emptying, which delays and blunts the peak substantially, and raises first-pass loss. The same drinks with a meal can give a peak a third lower.

pathways.name: Acetaldehyde
pathways.note: Toxic, reactive, and the immediate cause of flushing, nausea and much of the hangover. Normally destroyed within seconds by ALDH2. About 30-50% of people of East Asian descent carry an ALDH2 variant that works poorly, so acetaldehyde accumulates and causes the flush reaction — the same mechanism disulfiram induces deliberately.

pathways.name: Acetate
pathways.note: Harmless; enters normal metabolism and is burned as fuel, which is where alcohol's calories come from.

metabolism.secondary: CYP2E1 handles a growing share at high or chronic intake, and it is induced by regular drinking. That induction is what links heavy drinking to paracetamol liver injury.

effect_levels.label: 0.08% — the legal driving limit in much of the world
0.15% — clear intoxication, impaired balance and speech
0.35% — the range where respiratory depression becomes a real danger

female.note: Lower body-water fraction and less gastric ADH, so the same drinks give a noticeably higher peak at the same body weight.

chronic_heavy.note: CYP2E1 induction raises the elimination rate in regular heavy drinkers, up to about 0.03 %BAC/h. This is metabolic tolerance, and it is separate from the functional tolerance of the brain.

fed.note: Handled by choosing the 'with food' route.
